Package hadur2.core.gun

Class MainGun

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.gun.MainGun
public class MainGun extends Object
The main gun: a KNN displacement-vector gun with a kernel-density choice of angle.

Each past wave in its view stores where the target went as a displacement vector: its average movement per tick while the wave was in flight, in a frame turned to the target's heading and mirrored by its orbit direction (see Wave.displacementVector(hadur2.core.model.RobotState)). To aim, the gun finds the waves most like the present one, replays each neighbour's vector from the target's position and heading when the wave was made (normally this tick's scan) until a bullet fired from our next position would reach it, and takes the bearing to each projected point. It fires at the neighbour angle with the most other neighbour angles near it.

Replaying movement rather than a guess factor keeps the field's walls in the picture: a projected point outside the field is an impossible outcome and is dropped. The same view learns in melee (meleeOn), which is why it is the only gun used with several opponents.

Angles are absolute Robocode bearings in radians: 0 is north (+y), increasing clockwise. GunController calls aim(hadur2.core.model.Wave, hadur2.core.knn.KnnView<hadur2.core.model.TimestampedFiringAngle>, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long) on the aiming tick and for the main gun's virtual bullet.

    • aim

      public double aim(Wave w, KnnView<TimestampedFiringAngle> view, Point2D.Double myNextLocation, long currentTime)
      The absolute bearing to fire along, in radians.

      Each neighbour's projected angle is a candidate. A candidate's score is the sum over the other valid neighbours of weight * exp(-u^2 / 2), a Gaussian kernel with u the angle between them in units of the bandwidth; the bandwidth is twice 18 / distance, about the target's angular width. The best-scoring candidate wins; the first on a tie.

      Parameters:
      w - the gun wave for the shot, fired from our present position
      view - the main view for the target
      myNextLocation - where we will be when the bullet leaves, the next tick
      currentTime - the present tick
      Returns:
      the winning bearing in [0, 2pi), or w.absBearing (head-on from the wave's source, as atan2 gives it) when the view is empty or no neighbour gives a usable angle

    • aimWithMass

      public MainGun.Aimed aimWithMass(Wave w, KnnView<TimestampedFiringAngle> view, Point2D.Double myNextLocation, long currentTime)
      GUN-7: aim(hadur2.core.model.Wave, hadur2.core.knn.KnnView<hadur2.core.model.TimestampedFiringAngle>, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long) and the probability mass of the same aim, from one neighbour search: the angle is exactly aim's, and the mass is the kernel density of the neighbours that aim scored (valid ones, with their weights).
      Parameters:
      w - the gun wave for the shot
      view - the main view for the target
      myNextLocation - where we will be when the bullet leaves, the next tick
      currentTime - the present tick
      Returns:
      the angle and the mass; the mass is null when no neighbour is usable, in which case the angle is head-on

    • createView

      public KnnView<TimestampedFiringAngle> createView(int enemiesTotal)
      A new main view: the GunFormula space, k up to 100 at one neighbour per ten points, learning from every wave, virtual waves and melee waves included. It sets no size cap of its own, so it keeps KnnView.DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_POINTS (RES-2).
      Parameters:
      enemiesTotal - the opponents at the start of the battle, for the crowd feature
      Returns:
      the view, named viewName()
